suggestion_box:
## Suggestion box — file a grievance about the English

If any English string made you guess, file it. You are the only person who will ever
notice, and a string that made you guess will make the next 25 translators guess too.

File an entry when: the English has more than one plausible reading; a verb or adjective
has no stated object; a word's intended sense is not its most common sense; a term maps
onto a dangerous second sense in your language; a claim in the text looks false or stale;
or the tooling handed you a preferred_translation that is wrong for the context.

Report them in your final message as a JSON array, separate from your prose:

FRICTION: [
  {"key": "<lang key>", "complaint": "<what made you guess, in one sentence>",
   "readings": ["<reading you chose>", "<reading you rejected>"]}
]

An empty array is a fine and useful answer. Do NOT invent entries -- a false one costs a
human's attention. But do not stay quiet to be agreeable either: this channel exists
because real complaints were previously buried in prose and never acted on.

Where it goes and what happens next: the orchestrator copies each entry into
dev/english-friction/<sprint>.json, adds "source": "translator" and "lang": "<your
language code>", and answers it with a "disposition" plus a written "resolution" --
english (the English was rewritten), intent, glossary, dismissed (with the reason), or
refer-to-human. refer-to-human is a real answer and does NOT close the entry: escalating
is not resolving, and it stays visible until Tom rules on it. friction_check.php blocks
the sprint from CLOSING while any entry of yours is unanswered, so filing one is expected
work that the sprint waits on -- not a complaint about the sprint.
concept_source:
## Concepts are the source

Each concept is named in plain words, with its synonyms joined by "or". That plain name
is the authoritative source; the English term is one rendering of it, as yours will be.
Where key_concepts lists a concept for a key, translate the thing the plain name
describes, and give that concept the same word in every key that cites it. Where a
concept also has a definition, it is the author's own and outranks everything else.
Where a key has no key_concepts entry, the English is the source, as before.

uniqueness_attention lists the few groups of concepts that sit side by side on one
screen. Find unique names for each.

keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_scn_open_def:
The Scenario button in the status strip below the map names the open scenario and counts its overrides, as in Scenario: Base | No. of overrides: 0. Click it, or choose Water, Scenarios, to switch scenarios or to add, copy, rename, or delete one. Each scenario in the list shows its number of overrides in parentheses, and a check mark is at the open one. The Scenario manager row opens the tree of scenarios and alternatives, or only the list of scenarios while Basic mode is checked.

The drawing, the labels, Properties, Tables, and the results all belong to the open scenario, and the page solves the open scenario only. Scenario comparison, described in its own entry, solves the others from copies. The open scenario is saved with the project.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_scn_marks_def:
On the map, an asset that has an override in the open scenario is ringed in amber, and an asset that inherits an override from a parent scenario or alternative is ringed with a dashed gray line. For demand, diameter, roughness, minor (local) loss coefficient, and length, a ring appears only while Settings, Symbology, Node labels or Link labels shows that value on the map; an override of any other property always has its ring. In Tables, a cell that holds a value set by the open scenario is amber, and its tip names the alternative that holds it, as in Physical alt.: Larger main. Show scenarios, in the cell menu of a table, lists every asset once for each scenario.

Each row of Properties that a scenario can override has a mark at its left. A solid dot means the open scenario overrides the value; click it to clear the override. A hollow dot means the value is inherited; click it to make the value shown an override. A triangle means scenarios below this one override the value; click it to clear their overrides, after a confirmation. Beneath an overridden row is what Clear restores, as in Clear restores 18 in, the value in Base. The Settings box has the solid dot and the triangle only, because typing a value there is what makes an override.

To hide the rings, clear Show override markers on the map in Settings, Page, or choose Map, Clean map. Both are kept in this browser, not in the project. Tables marks overrides either way.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_scn_make_def:
With a scenario other than Base open, an edit to a value that scenarios can override is stored as an override in the open scenario, however it is made: typing in Properties, editing a cell in Tables, Replace in Find and replace, dragging a node or entering its coordinates, Morph (the new type is the override), or Paste properties to selection. A setting typed in the Settings box is stored as an override when scenarios can override that setting. Base is not changed. In Base, the same edits change the network itself and reach every scenario that has not overridden the value.

Delete acts differently. In a scenario, Delete does not remove an asset that exists in Base. It makes the asset inactive in the open scenario, and for a node also its pipes, and a message states this. The asset is still in the drawing and in the other scenarios. An asset drawn while a scenario is open is inactive in Base and active in that scenario, and Delete in that scenario removes it. Deleting an asset in Base also deletes its overrides in every scenario, after a question that counts them. A Shape follows the same rule as an asset. Customers belong to no scenario and are deleted outright.

The Override manager row of the Scenarios list opens a list of every override of the open scenario by category, each beside the inherited value it replaces. A time series graph on the map that the scenario opened, moved, or changed is a row of its own. Check rows and click Clear selected overrides, click Clear override in one row, or click Clear all overrides. Each value then returns to the inherited value, and Undo reverses it. Select an ID in the list to go to the asset on the map. The dot in Properties and the Clear override row in the cell menu of Tables clear one override at a time.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_scn_move_def: To move or merge elements from one scenario to another, open their Table, use the right-click context menu to Show scenarios, then set their Is active toggle and Clear override as desired in each scenario.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_scn_scope_def:
PropertiesEvery property of a node or link except those listed below, including its position, whether it is active, and its type (Morph). A Text can override its words, position, size, alignment, bold, angle, and whether it is shown. A Shape can override whether it is shown. A custom property can always be overridden. The properties are held in the categories Physical, Demand, Active topology, Initial settings, Constituent, Fire flow, Energy cost, Custom properties, Text, Presentation, and Calculation.
SettingsThe settings saved with the project, except those listed below: the calculation options (for example the demand multiplier, total run time, hydraulic time step, and friction method), the default demand pattern, the values given to new assets, and the presentation settings (sizes, colors, labels, contours, the map view, and the time series graphs on the map).
The same in every scenarioThe ID, Description, and Tag of an asset; the end nodes and bends of a link; Customers and the points of a Shape; the units and the coordinate system; and the contents of the Libraries (patterns, curves, pipe types, fittings lists, controls, and rules). An edit to any of these changes every scenario. A scenario can point an asset at a different curve, pipe type, fittings list, or pattern, but cannot change what is in them.

keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_scn_notes_def:
• An override equal to the inherited value is still an override. It is counted, and Override manager marks it (same).
  • Basic mode is a setting for this browser, not for the project. It is disabled for a project whose scenarios and alternatives it cannot show. Alternatives and the Scenario manager are described under How scenarios and alternatives work and How to manage scenarios, at the top of this entry.
  • Undo keeps 20 steps. Each step restores the scenarios and the open scenario along with the drawing, so adding, renaming, and deleting a scenario can be undone.
  • Exporting an EPANET file writes the open scenario only, with the values and node positions that scenario reads. The scenarios themselves are recorded in the project file only.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_cmp_cols_def:
ScenarioThe name of the scenario. The open scenario is marked (currently open).
No. of overridesThe overrides of the scenario itself, counted as in the Scenarios list. A calculation option such as the demand multiplier counts as one, and an override equal to the inherited value counts.
Demand multiplier, Total run time, Hydraulic time stepThe values the scenario was solved under, its own or those of the project. A steady-state scenario shows a dash for the time step.
Lowest pressure: Junction, Pressure, Time (hr)The lowest pressure at a junction, in three columns: the ID of the junction, the pressure, and the time it occurs. Reservoirs and tanks are left out because each has a fixed head.
Highest velocity: Link, Velocity, Time (hr)The highest velocity in a pipe or valve, in three columns: the ID of the link, the velocity, and the time it occurs. Pumps are left out.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_cmp_byasset_def: Below the table, Results by asset lists one row per asset of the type chosen in Asset type, with one column for each checked result in each scenario, for example the pressure at every junction in Base, Max day, and Peak hour. A scenario with a total run time is read at the time step on screen, or at its last time step if its run ends sooner, and each heading shows the time read. A scenario that cannot be solved keeps blank columns and a note that says why, and a scenario that did not converge is marked (not converged) in its headings. Copy puts the table on the clipboard as tab-separated text, ready to paste into a spreadsheet. Download CSV saves the same table as a file. Both carry the units in the headings and the numbers in full, without the rounding shown in the box. The sign of a flow is the solver's internal direction sign. It has no use outside the solver except to show in this table whether a flow changed direction between scenarios.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_cmp_notes_def:
• A scenario that cannot be solved shows the reason in place of its two results, for example that a junction has no path to a source after a pipe is made inactive. The other scenarios are still solved. A scenario that did not converge shows its last results and a message.
  • The block above the table, The same in every scenario, states the friction method, units, accuracy, and maximum trials. A setting that differs between scenarios is left out of the block.
  • There is no pass or fail threshold. Read the numbers against the design criteria of the system being modeled.
  • The example given in the Scenario manager entry compares scenarios on Net1.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_lib_kinds_def:
PatternsA list of multipliers that repeats for as long as a run lasts, one multiplier for each pattern time step. A new pattern is 24 multipliers of 1. Pasting a spreadsheet column fills the Multipliers box. The default demand pattern is marked (default) and is chosen in Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics.
CurvesFour kinds, chosen as the Curve type: Pump head, Pump efficiency, Tank volume, and Valve head loss. The points are entered in a grid that accepts a pasted spreadsheet column or lines copied from an EPANET file. A pump head curve with one point or with three points that begin at zero flow is fitted, and the Equation line shows the fit; one point is read as the design point, with a shutoff head of 1.33334 times its head and a maximum flow of 2 times its flow, as EPANET reads it. Any other pump head curve, and each of the other kinds, joins its points with straight lines. A pump or valve states its curve in Properties, where the last option in the curve list, Edit curves…, opens this section.
Pipe typesA definition of diameter, roughness, and reaction coefficients that several pipes refer to. A property may be left blank in the definition and then entered for each pipe. In Properties, the values a pipe type states are disabled, and Detach from pipe type copies them into the pipe and stops the pipe using the type.
FittingsLists of fittings with a quantity for each, added up to one minor (local) loss coefficient, k, for a pipe or pipe type. The fittings offered are the thirteen in Table 3.3 of the EPANET 2.2 user manual and Other fitting. Choosing one copies its coefficient into the row, where it can be changed.
ControlsOne statement each, in EPANET syntax, as in LINK id OPEN IF NODE id BELOW value. Under each, the box states whether it was understood.
RulesSeveral lines each, in EPANET syntax: RULE, IF, AND, OR, THEN, ELSE, and PRIORITY. Under each, the box states whether it was read.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_lib_import_def: File, Import…, Libraries… opens another project file and copies whole libraries from it into this project. An item whose name is already used here is skipped and listed, so nothing already here is changed. A warning is shown when the file and the project state a quantity in different units, and the items are imported as written. Pipe types that refer to a fittings list this project does not have are listed; import the fittings library from the same file to resolve them.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_prop_example_def:
Open the Net1 example and click Pipe 10. Properties lists its inputs, from Description to Active, and then its results at the time shown: Flow 1866.2 gpm, Velocity 2.4 ft/sec, and Head loss 19.12 ft H2O.

Click Pipe 113 and Shift-click Pipe 31. The title reads 2 selected, the one section is Pipes (2), and Diameter shows Various, because Pipe 31 is 6 in. and Pipe 113 is 8 in. Enter 10 for Diameter. The notice reads Set Diameter (in) on 2., both pipes are 10 in., and one Undo returns them to 6 and 8 in.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_set_where_def:
The list at the left of the box jumps to a section or a sub-heading. The sections are Symbology (Node labels, Node colors, Link labels, Link colors, Customer, and All), Map, Page, Assets (ID prefixes, Values, and Custom properties), Calculation (Units, Time, Hydraulics, Energy, and Quality), and Credits. Each sub-heading states whether its settings are Saved with the project or Saved in this browser. Everything is saved with the project except the settings under Page and one row in Hydraulics, Show the run progress box, which states Saved in this browser itself.

The Settings tab in Tables lists the same settings as rows, with their Category and Value, so a setting can also be found and audited there.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_bx_dock_def:
The corner of a box's title bar has Dock at the left of the map, Dock at the right of the map, and Float, and, once the box is docked, Auto-hide. A docked box is a column beside the map. With Auto-hide, it is a tab on a slim strip at the edge of the map. The tab opens the box on hover, after 150 ms with a mouse or pen, or on a click or tap. The box tucks back into its tab when the pointer has left it and focus is not inside it, when you press anywhere outside it, or when you press Esc. A tucked box is still open. A menu row or toolbar button that opens it brings it out of its tab.

Dragging a docked box by its title bar floats it and turns auto-hide off. Boxes docked on one side share one width, and the map keeps at least 320 px. Tabs are reordered by dragging them or by pressing Alt+Up or Alt+Down on a focused tab.

keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_ff_asks_def:
Each tested junction gets two tests, on a copy of the network at the time step on screen and in the open scenario. The first asks how much flow the junction can deliver while it holds the residual pressure. A flow is drawn at the junction, and repeated solves narrow it down, up to a ceiling equal to 10000 gpm. A junction that still holds the residual pressure at the ceiling is reported as delivering more than the ceiling. The second test, the design check, draws the required flow at the junction and asks whether any other junction in its scope falls below the Lowest system pressure allowed, or any pipe in its scope runs above the Highest velocity allowed. The design check is not made when its scope is None.

A junction with its own Required fire flow property is tested against that value, and every other junction against the value in the box.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_ff_dur_def: When the project has an extended-period simulation, choose A fire for a stated duration under Reporting step tested. The Required fire flow is then drawn at the one junction selected on the map, starting at the time in Fire starts at and lasting for the Fire duration, both whole multiples of the pattern time step. The whole simulation is run on a copy of the network and compared with the same simulation without the fire. The summary states whether the junction holds the Residual pressure to hold during the fire, the lowest pressure anywhere, whether any tank empties, and whether the system recovers after the fire. One table gives the lowest level of each tank, and another gives the pressure at the fire junction at every reporting step.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_cr_case_def: For each link in the scope, the link is made inactive on a copy of the network, and the copy is solved at the time step on screen in the open scenario. A run is one solve for each link and one more with nothing broken. A junction left with no open path to a reservoir or tank is cut off: it is removed before the solve, and its demand is counted as Demand not served. Of the junctions still connected, Junctions below minimum lists those whose pressure falls below the Lowest pressure allowed. A junction that is already below it with nothing broken is not counted against any link, and the summary states how many there are. Lowest pressure allowed is the same setting as the Lowest system pressure allowed box of the Fire flow analysis.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_ds_find_def: Find searches demand scales from 0 to 20, to the nearest 0.01, for the largest one at which every chosen junction keeps at least the Lowest pressure allowed. If the demands as entered already leave a junction below the limit, the answer is marked with a warning sign. If every junction keeps the limit at 20, the answer says so. Stop ends a search without an answer. Lowest pressure allowed is the same setting as the Lowest system pressure allowed box of the Fire flow analysis.

keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump curve is entered in Water, Libraries, as a Pump head curve, and the pump states that curve in Properties. Both solvers read it as EPANET reads it. One point uses EPANET’s rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33334 times the head entered, and the highest flow is 2 times the flow entered. A curve of one point and a curve of three points that begins at zero flow are fitted as H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it, and the Equation line shows the fit. A pump with no curve stated adds no head. The curve is not truncated where the head reaches zero, so a flow greater than the curve can deliver produces a negative head. keys_to_translate.lpn_sm_help:
How scenarios and alternatives work:

In Basic mode, alternatives are hidden and automatic, and all new scenarios are children of the Base scenario.

With Basic mode off, a complex inheritance tree is available, and alternatives can be shared among scenarios. But the default behavior of edits when a new alternative association is needed (in the absence of proactive user management) is to create an alternative named like the current scenario, which gives each scenario its unique set of alternatives.

Properties and settings belong to alternatives categories that appear as columns of the scenarios and alternatives table and as management options in Scenario manager.

Overrides are created in scenarios, but they really belong to the respective alternatives associated with the scenario; so a scenario is like a window to its alternatives. Associations of alternatives to scenarios are managed in the second pane of the Scenario manager or in the Scenarios table in the bottom pane. Creating a new scenario creates no alternatives; the new scenario uses its parent's alternatives until overrides are created that need new alternatives. When overrides are created in a scenario, they are stored in their respective alternative for the scenario; if the scenario has no such alternative, a new alternative is created using the name of the scenario.

Example: You create a "Figure: Node and link IDs" scenario and edit a Text to say "Node and Link IDs." When you create the scenario, no alternatives are created. But at the moment you save the Text, a Text alternative called "Figure: Node and link IDs" is created with the override for the Text value. In Basic mode, you see this as simply an override in the scenario itself.

Copy properties copies only overrides. In any scenario other than Base, it copies only the overrides the asset has in that scenario.

How to manage scenarios:

- Choose Scenarios or an alternatives category in the list at the top to show its tree.

- Create a child of the selected item with Add child. Add base adds another Base, which starts as a copy of Base as it is now; later edits to Base do not change it. A new child is named after its parent; type a name to rename it. Copy copies the selected alternative. Merge upward moves the overrides of the selected alternative into an alternative above it, chosen by name, and the selected alternative then inherits them; it first names any value an alternative it skips also overrides, which is not changed. To copy a scenario, use Copy scenario in the Scenarios menu, in Basic mode; it copies the scenario's overrides, with the alternatives that hold them. Add base and Copy scenario each create alternatives: Add base creates a Base alternative for the new Base in each category that holds values, and Copy scenario creates a new alternative, named like the copy, for each alternative that holds the scenario's overrides.

- Drag an item onto another to make it a child of that item. A scenario moved to a new parent inherits from it everything it has not overridden; what it has overridden does not change. Drag an item between two items to reorder them.

- Click an item to select it. Press F2 or choose Rename to rename the selected item. Renaming a scenario asks whether to rename the alternatives that carry its name; in Basic mode they are renamed with it, without asking. Double-click a scenario or press Enter to make it current. Click the arrow beside an item or press Left or Right to collapse or expand it. Right-click an item for the same commands as the buttons.

- Press Delete or click the minus button to delete the selected item. An item in use is not deleted, and the message names what uses it. Deleting a scenario with Basic mode off keeps the alternatives it uses. Deleting a scenario with Basic mode on also deletes each of its alternatives that no other scenario uses.

- To make a scenario use another alternative, including Base, choose it in the scenario's row of the second pane of the Scenario manager or the Scenarios table. An override made in a shared alternative changes every scenario that uses it.

keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_intro:
Each junction in turn draws a fire flow on top of its existing demand. The run uses a copy of the network at the time step on screen, so nothing in the project is changed.

When the project has an extended-period simulation, Reporting step tested selects the condition: the time step on screen, a chosen reporting step, the reporting step of lowest pressure among the junctions tested, or every reporting step. The last option runs the sweep at each reporting step with the tank levels, demand patterns, and link statuses of that step, and shows each junction at its own worst step, the step with the lowest available flow, in the Step of lowest flow column.

Fire flow is normally tested at maximum day demand, so set the network to that condition first.

Each junction tested takes about 16 solves of the whole network, so a large system takes minutes: choose the junctions before you run, and stop at any time to keep the partial results.

keys.lpn_guide_scn_open_def:
The Scenario button in the status strip below the map names the open scenario and counts its overrides, as in Scenario: Base | No. of overrides: 0. Click it, or choose Water, Scenarios, to switch scenarios or to add, copy, rename, or delete one. Each scenario in the list shows its number of overrides in parentheses, and a check mark is at the open one. The Scenario manager row opens the tree of scenarios and alternatives, or only the list of scenarios while Basic mode is checked.

The drawing, the labels, Properties, Tables, and the results all belong to the open scenario, and the page solves the open scenario only. Scenario comparison, described in its own entry, solves the others from copies. The open scenario is saved with the project.
keys.lpn_guide_scn_marks_def:
On the map, an asset that has an override in the open scenario is ringed in amber, and an asset that inherits an override from a parent scenario or alternative is ringed with a dashed gray line. For demand, diameter, roughness, minor (local) loss coefficient, and length, a ring appears only while Settings, Symbology, Node labels or Link labels shows that value on the map; an override of any other property always has its ring. In Tables, a cell that holds a value set by the open scenario is amber, and its tip names the alternative that holds it, as in Physical alt.: Larger main. Show scenarios, in the cell menu of a table, lists every asset once for each scenario.

Each row of Properties that a scenario can override has a mark at its left. A solid dot means the open scenario overrides the value; click it to clear the override. A hollow dot means the value is inherited; click it to make the value shown an override. A triangle means scenarios below this one override the value; click it to clear their overrides, after a confirmation. Beneath an overridden row is what Clear restores, as in Clear restores 18 in, the value in Base. The Settings box has the solid dot and the triangle only, because typing a value there is what makes an override.

To hide the rings, clear Show override markers on the map in Settings, Page, or choose Map, Clean map. Both are kept in this browser, not in the project. Tables marks overrides either way.
keys.lpn_guide_scn_make_def:
With a scenario other than Base open, an edit to a value that scenarios can override is stored as an override in the open scenario, however it is made: typing in Properties, editing a cell in Tables, Replace in Find and replace, dragging a node or entering its coordinates, Morph (the new type is the override), or Paste properties to selection. A setting typed in the Settings box is stored as an override when scenarios can override that setting. Base is not changed. In Base, the same edits change the network itself and reach every scenario that has not overridden the value.

Delete acts differently. In a scenario, Delete does not remove an asset that exists in Base. It makes the asset inactive in the open scenario, and for a node also its pipes, and a message states this. The asset is still in the drawing and in the other scenarios. An asset drawn while a scenario is open is inactive in Base and active in that scenario, and Delete in that scenario removes it. Deleting an asset in Base also deletes its overrides in every scenario, after a question that counts them. A Shape follows the same rule as an asset. Customers belong to no scenario and are deleted outright.

The Override manager row of the Scenarios list opens a list of every override of the open scenario by category, each beside the inherited value it replaces. A time series graph on the map that the scenario opened, moved, or changed is a row of its own. Check rows and click Clear selected overrides, click Clear override in one row, or click Clear all overrides. Each value then returns to the inherited value, and Undo reverses it. Select an ID in the list to go to the asset on the map. The dot in Properties and the Clear override row in the cell menu of Tables clear one override at a time.
keys.lpn_guide_scn_move_def: To move or merge elements from one scenario to another, open their Table, use the right-click context menu to Show scenarios, then set their Is active toggle and Clear override as desired in each scenario.
keys.lpn_guide_scn_scope_def:
PropertiesEvery property of a node or link except those listed below, including its position, whether it is active, and its type (Morph). A Text can override its words, position, size, alignment, bold, angle, and whether it is shown. A Shape can override whether it is shown. A custom property can always be overridden. The properties are held in the categories Physical, Demand, Active topology, Initial settings, Constituent, Fire flow, Energy cost, Custom properties, Text, Presentation, and Calculation.
SettingsThe settings saved with the project, except those listed below: the calculation options (for example the demand multiplier, total run time, hydraulic time step, and friction method), the default demand pattern, the values given to new assets, and the presentation settings (sizes, colors, labels, contours, the map view, and the time series graphs on the map).
The same in every scenarioThe ID, Description, and Tag of an asset; the end nodes and bends of a link; Customers and the points of a Shape; the units and the coordinate system; and the contents of the Libraries (patterns, curves, pipe types, fittings lists, controls, and rules). An edit to any of these changes every scenario. A scenario can point an asset at a different curve, pipe type, fittings list, or pattern, but cannot change what is in them.

keys.lpn_guide_scn_notes_def:
• An override equal to the inherited value is still an override. It is counted, and Override manager marks it (same).
  • Basic mode is a setting for this browser, not for the project. It is disabled for a project whose scenarios and alternatives it cannot show. Alternatives and the Scenario manager are described under How scenarios and alternatives work and How to manage scenarios, at the top of this entry.
  • Undo keeps 20 steps. Each step restores the scenarios and the open scenario along with the drawing, so adding, renaming, and deleting a scenario can be undone.
  • Exporting an EPANET file writes the open scenario only, with the values and node positions that scenario reads. The scenarios themselves are recorded in the project file only.
keys.lpn_guide_cmp_cols_def:
ScenarioThe name of the scenario. The open scenario is marked (currently open).
No. of overridesThe overrides of the scenario itself, counted as in the Scenarios list. A calculation option such as the demand multiplier counts as one, and an override equal to the inherited value counts.
Demand multiplier, Total run time, Hydraulic time stepThe values the scenario was solved under, its own or those of the project. A steady-state scenario shows a dash for the time step.
Lowest pressure: Junction, Pressure, Time (hr)The lowest pressure at a junction, in three columns: the ID of the junction, the pressure, and the time it occurs. Reservoirs and tanks are left out because each has a fixed head.
Highest velocity: Link, Velocity, Time (hr)The highest velocity in a pipe or valve, in three columns: the ID of the link, the velocity, and the time it occurs. Pumps are left out.
keys.lpn_guide_cmp_byasset_def: Below the table, Results by asset lists one row per asset of the type chosen in Asset type, with one column for each checked result in each scenario, for example the pressure at every junction in Base, Max day, and Peak hour. A scenario with a total run time is read at the time step on screen, or at its last time step if its run ends sooner, and each heading shows the time read. A scenario that cannot be solved keeps blank columns and a note that says why, and a scenario that did not converge is marked (not converged) in its headings. Copy puts the table on the clipboard as tab-separated text, ready to paste into a spreadsheet. Download CSV saves the same table as a file. Both carry the units in the headings and the numbers in full, without the rounding shown in the box. The sign of a flow is the solver's internal direction sign. It has no use outside the solver except to show in this table whether a flow changed direction between scenarios.
keys.lpn_guide_cmp_notes_def:
• A scenario that cannot be solved shows the reason in place of its two results, for example that a junction has no path to a source after a pipe is made inactive. The other scenarios are still solved. A scenario that did not converge shows its last results and a message.
  • The block above the table, The same in every scenario, states the friction method, units, accuracy, and maximum trials. A setting that differs between scenarios is left out of the block.
  • There is no pass or fail threshold. Read the numbers against the design criteria of the system being modeled.
  • The example given in the Scenario manager entry compares scenarios on Net1.
keys.lpn_guide_lib_kinds_def:
PatternsA list of multipliers that repeats for as long as a run lasts, one multiplier for each pattern time step. A new pattern is 24 multipliers of 1. Pasting a spreadsheet column fills the Multipliers box. The default demand pattern is marked (default) and is chosen in Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics.
CurvesFour kinds, chosen as the Curve type: Pump head, Pump efficiency, Tank volume, and Valve head loss. The points are entered in a grid that accepts a pasted spreadsheet column or lines copied from an EPANET file. A pump head curve with one point or with three points that begin at zero flow is fitted, and the Equation line shows the fit; one point is read as the design point, with a shutoff head of 1.33334 times its head and a maximum flow of 2 times its flow, as EPANET reads it. Any other pump head curve, and each of the other kinds, joins its points with straight lines. A pump or valve states its curve in Properties, where the last option in the curve list, Edit curves…, opens this section.
Pipe typesA definition of diameter, roughness, and reaction coefficients that several pipes refer to. A property may be left blank in the definition and then entered for each pipe. In Properties, the values a pipe type states are disabled, and Detach from pipe type copies them into the pipe and stops the pipe using the type.
FittingsLists of fittings with a quantity for each, added up to one minor (local) loss coefficient, k, for a pipe or pipe type. The fittings offered are the thirteen in Table 3.3 of the EPANET 2.2 user manual and Other fitting. Choosing one copies its coefficient into the row, where it can be changed.
ControlsOne statement each, in EPANET syntax, as in LINK id OPEN IF NODE id BELOW value. Under each, the box states whether it was understood.
RulesSeveral lines each, in EPANET syntax: RULE, IF, AND, OR, THEN, ELSE, and PRIORITY. Under each, the box states whether it was read.
keys.lpn_guide_lib_import_def: File, Import…, Libraries… opens another project file and copies whole libraries from it into this project. An item whose name is already used here is skipped and listed, so nothing already here is changed. A warning is shown when the file and the project state a quantity in different units, and the items are imported as written. Pipe types that refer to a fittings list this project does not have are listed; import the fittings library from the same file to resolve them.
keys.lpn_guide_prop_example_def:
Open the Net1 example and click Pipe 10. Properties lists its inputs, from Description to Active, and then its results at the time shown: Flow 1866.2 gpm, Velocity 2.4 ft/sec, and Head loss 19.12 ft H2O.

Click Pipe 113 and Shift-click Pipe 31. The title reads 2 selected, the one section is Pipes (2), and Diameter shows Various, because Pipe 31 is 6 in. and Pipe 113 is 8 in. Enter 10 for Diameter. The notice reads Set Diameter (in) on 2., both pipes are 10 in., and one Undo returns them to 6 and 8 in.
keys.lpn_guide_set_where_def:
The list at the left of the box jumps to a section or a sub-heading. The sections are Symbology (Node labels, Node colors, Link labels, Link colors, Customer, and All), Map, Page, Assets (ID prefixes, Values, and Custom properties), Calculation (Units, Time, Hydraulics, Energy, and Quality), and Credits. Each sub-heading states whether its settings are Saved with the project or Saved in this browser. Everything is saved with the project except the settings under Page and one row in Hydraulics, Show the run progress box, which states Saved in this browser itself.

The Settings tab in Tables lists the same settings as rows, with their Category and Value, so a setting can also be found and audited there.
keys.lpn_guide_bx_dock_def:
The corner of a box's title bar has Dock at the left of the map, Dock at the right of the map, and Float, and, once the box is docked, Auto-hide. A docked box is a column beside the map. With Auto-hide, it is a tab on a slim strip at the edge of the map. The tab opens the box on hover, after 150 ms with a mouse or pen, or on a click or tap. The box tucks back into its tab when the pointer has left it and focus is not inside it, when you press anywhere outside it, or when you press Esc. A tucked box is still open. A menu row or toolbar button that opens it brings it out of its tab.

Dragging a docked box by its title bar floats it and turns auto-hide off. Boxes docked on one side share one width, and the map keeps at least 320 px. Tabs are reordered by dragging them or by pressing Alt+Up or Alt+Down on a focused tab.
keys.lpn_guide_bx_phone_def: At 640 px or narrower, a docked box is always an auto-hide tab, and it flies out over the map. Nothing is pinned. A box that is not docked fills the window.
keys.lpn_guide_ff_asks_def:
Each tested junction gets two tests, on a copy of the network at the time step on screen and in the open scenario. The first asks how much flow the junction can deliver while it holds the residual pressure. A flow is drawn at the junction, and repeated solves narrow it down, up to a ceiling equal to 10000 gpm. A junction that still holds the residual pressure at the ceiling is reported as delivering more than the ceiling. The second test, the design check, draws the required flow at the junction and asks whether any other junction in its scope falls below the Lowest system pressure allowed, or any pipe in its scope runs above the Highest velocity allowed. The design check is not made when its scope is None.

A junction with its own Required fire flow property is tested against that value, and every other junction against the value in the box.
keys.lpn_guide_ff_dur_def: When the project has an extended-period simulation, choose A fire for a stated duration under Reporting step tested. The Required fire flow is then drawn at the one junction selected on the map, starting at the time in Fire starts at and lasting for the Fire duration, both whole multiples of the pattern time step. The whole simulation is run on a copy of the network and compared with the same simulation without the fire. The summary states whether the junction holds the Residual pressure to hold during the fire, the lowest pressure anywhere, whether any tank empties, and whether the system recovers after the fire. One table gives the lowest level of each tank, and another gives the pressure at the fire junction at every reporting step.
keys.lpn_guide_cr_case_def: For each link in the scope, the link is made inactive on a copy of the network, and the copy is solved at the time step on screen in the open scenario. A run is one solve for each link and one more with nothing broken. A junction left with no open path to a reservoir or tank is cut off: it is removed before the solve, and its demand is counted as Demand not served. Of the junctions still connected, Junctions below minimum lists those whose pressure falls below the Lowest pressure allowed. A junction that is already below it with nothing broken is not counted against any link, and the summary states how many there are. Lowest pressure allowed is the same setting as the Lowest system pressure allowed box of the Fire flow analysis.
keys.lpn_guide_ds_find_def: Find searches demand scales from 0 to 20, to the nearest 0.01, for the largest one at which every chosen junction keeps at least the Lowest pressure allowed. It reports the scale and the lowest pressure there, and the same for the next step up, where the pressure first falls below the limit. If the demands as entered already leave a junction below the limit, the answer is marked with a warning sign. If every junction keeps the limit at 20, the answer says so. Stop ends a search without an answer. Lowest pressure allowed is the same setting as the Lowest system pressure allowed box of the Fire flow analysis.
keys.lpn_guide_ct_box_def: Show plot, when cleared, hides the fill and the lines and keeps the node colors. The box also holds Color nodes by and Color scheme, which are the same two settings as in Settings, Symbology, Node colors, the Fill (None, Smooth, or Bands, which paints each class flat), the Fill opacity, the Contour lines with their Interval and Labels, and the Buffer (× median pipe length). In a project placed on the Earth, the box can also take the ground between nodes from Mapbox DEM, after the visitor agrees to send the tile numbers of the network's area. These settings are saved with the project and can be overridden by a scenario. The plot changes only the display, not the network.
keys.lpn_guide_ct_example_def: Open the Net1 example and choose Water, Graphs, Contour. The nodes are colored by pressure, and the line under the color key states 9 nodes, 11 pipes, a reach of 2.5 times the median pipe length beside them, and lines every 5 psi. keys.lpn_guide_fr_what_def: Choose Water, Reports, Full. The table has one row for each node and link at each reporting time step, in the units of the Tables pane. The Time step list chooses the step shown, and Download CSV, Copy HTML, and Print report carry every step. Without an extended period simulation, the table shows the current solution at one instant.

keys.lpn_notes_1_def: By default the network is solved by the EPANET solver. With Use the built-in solver when possible checked, a single instant solution can be solved by the built-in solver instead, but an extended period simulation is always solved by the EPANET solver.
keys.lpn_notes_2_def: Surge and water hammer are not modeled: all results are for steady or slowly varying flow, not for the transient pressure wave caused by rapid valve closure. Multi-species water quality (EPANET-MSX) is not modeled. Water age, source trace, and one reacting chemical are.
keys.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump curve is entered in Water, Libraries, as a Pump head curve, and the pump states that curve in Properties. Both solvers read it as EPANET reads it. One point uses EPANET’s rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33334 times the head entered, and the highest flow is 2 times the flow entered. A curve of one point and a curve of three points that begins at zero flow are fitted as H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it, and the Equation line shows the fit. Any other curve (two points, three points that do not begin at zero flow, or four or more points) is used as straight lines between its points, and the first and last lines are extended beyond the ends of the curve. A pump with no curve stated adds no head. The curve is not truncated where the head reaches zero, so a flow greater than the curve can deliver produces a negative head. The remedy is a larger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve.

keys.lpn_sm_help:
How scenarios and alternatives work:

In Basic mode, alternatives are hidden and automatic, and all new scenarios are children of the Base scenario.

With Basic mode off, a complex inheritance tree is available, and alternatives can be shared among scenarios. But the default behavior of edits when a new alternative association is needed (in the absence of proactive user management) is to create an alternative named like the current scenario, which gives each scenario its unique set of alternatives.

Properties and settings belong to alternatives categories that appear as columns of the scenarios and alternatives table and as management options in Scenario manager.

Overrides are created in scenarios, but they really belong to the respective alternatives associated with the scenario; so a scenario is like a window to its alternatives. Associations of alternatives to scenarios are managed in the second pane of the Scenario manager or in the Scenarios table in the bottom pane. Creating a new scenario creates no alternatives; the new scenario uses its parent's alternatives until overrides are created that need new alternatives. When overrides are created in a scenario, they are stored in their respective alternative for the scenario; if the scenario has no such alternative, a new alternative is created using the name of the scenario.

Example: You create a "Figure: Node and link IDs" scenario and edit a Text to say "Node and Link IDs." When you create the scenario, no alternatives are created. But at the moment you save the Text, a Text alternative called "Figure: Node and link IDs" is created with the override for the Text value. In Basic mode, you see this as simply an override in the scenario itself.

Copy properties copies only overrides. In any scenario other than Base, it copies only the overrides the asset has in that scenario.

How to manage scenarios:

- Choose Scenarios or an alternatives category in the list at the top to show its tree.

- Create a child of the selected item with Add child. Add base adds another Base, which starts as a copy of Base as it is now; later edits to Base do not change it. A new child is named after its parent; type a name to rename it. Copy copies the selected alternative. Merge upward moves the overrides of the selected alternative into an alternative above it, chosen by name, and the selected alternative then inherits them; it first names any value an alternative it skips also overrides, which is not changed. To copy a scenario, use Copy scenario in the Scenarios menu, in Basic mode; it copies the scenario's overrides, with the alternatives that hold them. Add base and Copy scenario each create alternatives: Add base creates a Base alternative for the new Base in each category that holds values, and Copy scenario creates a new alternative, named like the copy, for each alternative that holds the scenario's overrides.

- Drag an item onto another to make it a child of that item. A scenario moved to a new parent inherits from it everything it has not overridden; what it has overridden does not change. Drag an item between two items to reorder them.

- Click an item to select it. Press F2 or choose Rename to rename the selected item. Renaming a scenario asks whether to rename the alternatives that carry its name; in Basic mode they are renamed with it, without asking. Double-click a scenario or press Enter to make it current. Click the arrow beside an item or press Left or Right to collapse or expand it. Right-click an item for the same commands as the buttons.

- Press Delete or click the minus button to delete the selected item. An item in use is not deleted, and the message names what uses it. Deleting a scenario with Basic mode off keeps the alternatives it uses. Deleting a scenario with Basic mode on also deletes each of its alternatives that no other scenario uses.

- To make a scenario use another alternative, including Base, choose it in the scenario's row of the second pane of the Scenario manager or the Scenarios table. An override made in a shared alternative changes every scenario that uses it.

keys.lpn_ff_intro:
Each junction in turn draws a fire flow on top of its existing demand. The run uses a copy of the network at the time step on screen, so nothing in the project is changed.

When the project has an extended-period simulation, Reporting step tested selects the condition: the time step on screen, a chosen reporting step, the reporting step of lowest pressure among the junctions tested, or every reporting step. The last option runs the sweep at each reporting step with the tank levels, demand patterns, and link statuses of that step, and shows each junction at its own worst step, the step with the lowest available flow, in the Step of lowest flow column.

Fire flow is normally tested at maximum day demand, so set the network to that condition first.

Each junction tested takes about 16 solves of the whole network, so a large system takes minutes: choose the junctions before you run, and stop at any time to keep the partial results.

The system counts as recovered when, at the last reporting step, no junction is more than about 0.14 psi (1 kPa) and no tank more than about 0.3 ft (0.1 m) from the run without the fire.

keys.lpn_ds_intro:

حين يكون مفتوحاً سيناريو غير الأساس، يُخزَّن أي تعديل لقيمة يمكن للسيناريوهات تجاوزها تجاوزاً في السيناريو المفتوح، أياً كانت طريقته: الكتابة في الخصائص، أو تعديل خلية في الجداول، أو استبدال في البحث والاستبدال، أو سحب عقدة أو إدخال إحداثياتها، أو تغيير النوع (النوع الجديد هو التجاوز)، أو لصق الخصائص في التحديد. ويُخزَّن الإعداد المكتوب في مربع الإعدادات تجاوزاً حين يمكن للسيناريوهات تجاوز ذلك الإعداد. ولا يتغير الأساس. وفي الأساس تغيّر التعديلات نفسها الشبكة ذاتها وتصل إلى كل سيناريو لم يتجاوز القيمة.

يختلف الحذف في سلوكه. ففي سيناريو، لا يزيل الحذف عنصراً موجوداً في الأساس. بل يجعل العنصر غير فعّال في السيناريو المفتوح، وكذلك أنابيبه إن كان عقدة، وتذكر رسالة ذلك. ويبقى العنصر في الرسم وفي السيناريوهات الأخرى. والعنصر المرسوم والسيناريو مفتوح غير فعّال في الأساس وفعّال في ذلك السيناريو، ويزيله الحذف في ذلك السيناريو. ويحذف حذف عنصر في الأساس تجاوزاته في كل سيناريو أيضاً، بعد سؤال يعدّها. أما المشتركون والأشكال فلا تنتمي إلى أي سيناريو وتُحذف حذفاً تاماً.

يفتح الصف مدير التجاوزات في قائمة السيناريوهات قائمة بكل تجاوزات السيناريو المفتوح حسب الفئة، كل منها بجانب القيمة الموروثة التي يحل محلها. ورسم السلسلة الزمنية على الخريطة الذي فتحه السيناريو أو نقله أو غيّره صف مستقل. علّم الصفوف وانقر على مسح التجاوزات المحددة، أو انقر على مسح التجاوز في صف واحد، أو انقر على مسح كل التجاوزات. فتعود كل قيمة إلى القيمة الموروثة، ويعكس تراجع ذلك. اختر معرّفاً في القائمة للانتقال إلى العنصر على الخريطة. وتمسح النقطة في الخصائص وصف مسح التجاوز في قائمة خلية الجداول تجاوزاً واحداً في كل مرة.

With a scenario other than Base open, an edit to a value that scenarios can override is stored as an override in the open scenario, however it is made: typing in Properties, editing a cell in Tables, Replace in Find and replace, dragging a node or entering its coordinates, Morph (the new type is the override), or Paste properties to selection. A setting typed in the Settings box is stored as an override when scenarios can override that setting. Base is not changed. In Base, the same edits change the network itself and reach every scenario that has not overridden the value.

Delete acts differently. In a scenario, Delete does not remove an asset that exists in Base. It makes the asset inactive in the open scenario, and for a node also its pipes, and a message states this. The asset is still in the drawing and in the other scenarios. An asset drawn while a scenario is open is inactive in Base and active in that scenario, and Delete in that scenario removes it. Deleting an asset in Base also deletes its overrides in every scenario, after a question that counts them. A Shape follows the same rule as an asset. Customers belong to no scenario and are deleted outright.

The Override manager row of the Scenarios list opens a list of every override of the open scenario by category, each beside the inherited value it replaces. A time series graph on the map that the scenario opened, moved, or changed is a row of its own. Check rows and click Clear selected overrides, click Clear override in one row, or click Clear all overrides. Each value then returns to the inherited value, and Undo reverses it. Select an ID in the list to go to the asset on the map. The dot in Properties and the Clear override row in the cell menu of Tables clear one override at a time.

يختلف الحذف في سلوكه. ففي سيناريو، لا يزيل الحذف عنصراً موجوداً في الأساس. بل يجعل العنصر غير فعّال في السيناريو المفتوح، وكذلك أنابيبه إن كان عقدة، وتذكر رسالة ذلك. ويبقى العنصر في الرسم وفي السيناريوهات الأخرى. والعنصر المرسوم والسيناريو مفتوح غير فعّال في الأساس وفعّال في ذلك السيناريو، ويزيله الحذف في ذلك السيناريو. ويحذف حذف عنصر في الأساس تجاوزاته في كل سيناريو أيضاً، بعد سؤال يعدّها. أما المشتركون والأشكال فلا تنتمي إلى أي سيناريو وتُحذف حذفاً تاماً.

يفتح الصف مدير التجاوزات في قائمة السيناريوهات قائمة بكل تجاوزات السيناريو المفتوح حسب الفئة، كل منها بجانب القيمة الموروثة التي يحل محلها. ورسم السلسلة الزمنية على الخريطة الذي فتحه السيناريو أو نقله أو غيّره صف مستقل. علّم الصفوف وانقر على مسح التجاوزات المحددة، أو انقر على مسح التجاوز في صف واحد، أو انقر على مسح كل التجاوزات. فتعود كل قيمة إلى القيمة الموروثة، ويعكس تراجع ذلك. اختر معرّفاً في القائمة للانتقال إلى العنصر على الخريطة. وتمسح النقطة في الخصائص وصف مسح التجاوز في قائمة خلية الجداول تجاوزاً واحداً في كل مرة.

With a scenario other than Base open, an edit to a value that scenarios can override is stored as an override in the open scenario, however it is made: typing in Properties, editing a cell in Tables, Replace in Find and replace, dragging a node or entering its coordinates, Morph (the new type is the override), or Paste properties to selection. A setting typed in the Settings box is stored as an override when scenarios can override that setting. Base is not changed. In Base, the same edits change the network itself and reach every scenario that has not overridden the value.

Delete acts differently. In a scenario, Delete does not remove an asset that exists in Base. It makes the asset inactive in the open scenario, and for a node also its pipes, and a message states this. The asset is still in the drawing and in the other scenarios. An asset drawn while a scenario is open is inactive in Base and active in that scenario, and Delete in that scenario removes it. Deleting an asset in Base also deletes its overrides in every scenario, after a question that counts them. A Shape follows the same rule as an asset. Customers belong to no scenario and are deleted outright.

The Override manager row of the Scenarios list opens a list of every override of the open scenario by category, each beside the inherited value it replaces. A time series graph on the map that the scenario opened, moved, or changed is a row of its own. Check rows and click Clear selected overrides, click Clear override in one row, or click Clear all overrides. Each value then returns to the inherited value, and Undo reverses it. Select an ID in the list to go to the asset on the map. The dot in Properties and the Clear override row in the cell menu of Tables clear one override at a time.

lpn_notes_1_def.current_value: تُحَلّ الشبكة افتراضياً بحلّال EPANET. وعند ضبط مدة تشغيل كلية، تُحسب كل خطوة زمنية للإبلاغ بالتتابع: تمتلئ الصهاريج وتفرغ، وتتبع الطلبات أنماطها، ويعيد شريط الأدوات عرض التشغيل. ومع تعليم استخدم الحلّال المدمج حيثما أمكن، يمكن أن يحل الحلّال المدمج حلّ لحظة واحدة بدلاً منه، لكن محاكاة الفترة الممتدة أو الشبكة التي فيها صمام كاسر للضغط أو صمام عام الغرض (PBV، GPV) تُحلّ دائماً بحلّال EPANET.

lpn_notes_5_def.current_value: تتبع المضخة العلاقة H = H₀ − aQ^b، حيث H هو العلو الذي تضيفه المضخة وQ هو التدفق خلالها. وتُدخل نقاط المنحنى في المياه، المكتبات، بوصفها منحنى علو مضخة، وتذكر المضخة ذلك المنحنى في الخصائص. النقاط الثلاث، وهي العلو عند تدفق صفري ونقطة التشغيل العادية ونقطة أعلى تدفق، توائم H₀ وa وb مباشرة، وتتبع المنحنى المنشور عن كثب. وتوائم النقطتان قطعاً مكافئاً (b = 2) قمته عند تدفق صفري. وتستخدم النقطة الواحدة قاعدة EPANET: العلو عند تدفق صفري يساوي 1.33334 ضعف العلو المُدخل، وأعلى تدفق يساوي ضعف التدفق المُدخل، مما يعطي أيضاً b = 2. والمضخة التي لا منحنى لها لا تضيف أي علو. ولا يُقطع المنحنى عند وصول العلو إلى الصفر، لذا فإن تدفقاً أكبر مما يستطيع المنحنى تقديمه يعطي علواً سالباً. والحل مضخة أكبر أو طلب أصغر، لا موائمة منحنى مختلفة. ويمكن للمنحنى أن يحمل أكثر من ثلاث نقاط. فيُعطى حلّال EPANET كلها ويستكمل بينها، بينما يستخدم سطر المعادلة والحلّال المدمج أدنى النقاط ووسطاها وأعلاها.

lpn_sm_help.current_value:
كيف تعمل السيناريوهات والبدائل:

في الوضع الأساسي تكون البدائل مخفية وتلقائية، وتكون كل السيناريوهات الجديدة فرعية للسيناريو الأساس.

ومع إيقاف الوضع الأساسي تتوفر شجرة وراثة معقدة، ويمكن مشاركة البدائل بين السيناريوهات. لكن السلوك الافتراضي للتعديلات حين تلزم صلة بديل جديدة (في غياب إدارة استباقية من المستخدم) هو إنشاء بديل يحمل اسماً مثل اسم السيناريو الحالي، فيكون لكل سيناريو مجموعته الفريدة من البدائل.

تنتمي الخصائص والإعدادات إلى فئات بدائل تظهر أعمدة في جدول السيناريوهات والبدائل وخيارات إدارة في مدير السيناريوهات.

تُنشأ التجاوزات في السيناريوهات، لكنها تنتمي فعلاً إلى البدائل المرتبطة بالسيناريو؛ فالسيناريو كنافذة على بدائله. وتُدار صلات البدائل بالسيناريوهات في اللوحة اليمنى من مدير السيناريوهات أو في جدول السيناريوهات في اللوحة السفلية. وإنشاء سيناريو جديد لا ينشئ بدائل؛ يستخدم السيناريو الجديد بدائل أصله إلى أن تُنشأ تجاوزات تحتاج إلى بدائل جديدة. وحين تُنشأ تجاوزات في سيناريو تُخزَّن في بديلها المقابل للسيناريو؛ فإن لم يكن للسيناريو بديل كهذا يُنشأ بديل جديد باسم السيناريو.

مثال: تنشئ سيناريو «Figure: Node and link IDs» وتعدّل نصاً ليقول «Node and Link IDs». عند إنشاء السيناريو لا تُنشأ بدائل. لكن لحظة حفظ النص يُنشأ بديل نص اسمه «Figure: Node and link IDs» مع التجاوز لقيمة النص. وفي الوضع الأساسي ترى ذلك تجاوزاً في السيناريو نفسه فحسب.

ينسخ نسخ الخصائص التجاوزات فقط. وفي أي سيناريو غير الأساس ينسخ التجاوزات التي للعنصر في ذلك السيناريو فقط.

كيف تدير السيناريوهات:

- اختر السيناريوهات أو فئة بدائل في القائمة في الأعلى لعرض شجرتها.

- أنشئ فرعاً للعنصر المحدد بإضافة عنصر فرعي. وتضيف إضافة أساس أساساً آخر، يبدأ نسخة من الأساس كما هو الآن؛ ولا تغيّره التعديلات اللاحقة على الأساس. ويُسمّى الفرع الجديد باسم أصله؛ اكتب اسماً لإعادة تسميته. وينسخ نسخ البديل المحدد. ويدمج دمج إلى الأعلى تجاوزات البديل المحدد في بديل فوقه، يُختار بالاسم، فيرثها البديل المحدد بعد ذلك؛ ويسمّي أولاً أي قيمة يتجاوزها أيضاً بديل يتخطاه، وهي لا تتغير. ولنسخ سيناريو، استخدم نسخ السيناريو في قائمة السيناريوهات، في الوضع الأساسي؛ وهو ينسخ تجاوزات السيناريو، مع البدائل التي تحملها. وتنشئ إضافة أساس ونسخ السيناريو كلتاهما بدائل: تنشئ إضافة أساس بديل أساس للأساس الجديد في كل فئة تحمل قيماً، وينشئ نسخ السيناريو بديلاً جديداً، باسم النسخة، لكل بديل يحمل تجاوزات السيناريو.

- اسحب عنصراً على آخر لجعله فرعاً لذلك العنصر. والسيناريو المنقول إلى أصل جديد يرث منه كل ما لم يتجاوزه؛ وما تجاوزه لا يتغير. واسحب عنصراً بين عنصرين لإعادة ترتيبهما.

- انقر عنصراً لتحديده. اضغط F2 أو اختر إعادة تسمية لإعادة تسمية العنصر المحدد. وتسأل إعادة تسمية سيناريو هل تُعاد تسمية البدائل التي تحمل اسمه؛ وفي الوضع الأساسي تُعاد تسميتها معه دون سؤال. وانقر مرتين على سيناريو أو اضغط Enter لجعله الحالي. وانقر السهم بجانب عنصر أو اضغط اليسار أو اليمين لطيّه أو توسيعه. وانقر بزر الفأرة الأيمن عنصراً للحصول على الأوامر نفسها التي في الأزرار.

- اضغط Delete أو انقر زر الناقص لحذف العنصر المحدد. ولا يُحذف عنصر قيد الاستخدام، وتسمّي الرسالة ما يستخدمه. وحذف سيناريو مع إيقاف الوضع الأساسي يُبقي البدائل التي يستخدمها. وحذف سيناريو مع تشغيل الوضع الأساسي يحذف أيضاً كل بديل له لا يستخدمه سيناريو آخر.

- لجعل سيناريو يستخدم بديلاً آخر، ومنه الأساس، اخترْه في صف السيناريو في اللوحة اليمنى من مدير السيناريوهات أو في جدول السيناريوهات. والتجاوز الذي يُجرى في بديل مشترك يغيّر كل سيناريو يستخدمه.

lpn_demand_cats: Layout (box title): The title of a box that can be docked and set to auto-hide. Tucked away, the box shows only the start of its title, on a narrow tab at the map's edge turned on its side, cut off after about 12 to 25 characters. Put the word that names the box's subject first, so each tab can be told from its neighbors; a title form with a colon is fine (Pump energy report, in Spanish: Bombas: informe de energía). Where the natural phrase already starts with that word, keep it. The same text may also be a menu row.
